build: XPB disk, Scratch of Triangle directory

exclude: All 1000 cells are KERNAL screen spaces at match entry. Match setup replaces them with generated workspace.
Matches the pre-match menu byte for byte. Contains the tail of its draft text. The part uses the upper pages for generated screen cells and pointers.
Seven parked menu pages. Live pre-load capture matches $0800-$0EFF byte for byte after the swap at $FFCE. Menu-authored bytes count in the menu listing.
Remaining packed menu backdrop at match entry, identical to the pre-match snapshot. Match scroll code and the sprite compositor write the second screen and sprite workspace here.
extra: Full file B payload matched byte for byte in the match hand-over
File G school map and court data, matched byte for byte in the hand-over
File C school character data copied here from $1800 before the game starts
File K payload matched byte for byte in the match hand-over
Authored file A material left after B overwrites RAM through $69FF. Includes both sprite catalogues and pose data.
File A material still present after the selected G-style court map covers $C000-$C57F.

comments.text: Saves the numeric file selector from X. Adds $40 to make the PETSCII name, exposes the KERNAL, sets a one-character name and calls LOAD for device 8 with secondary address 2. Restores banking on return.
Three $EA bytes precede the disk loader's entry at $0E03.
The loader enters here after loading B. The trampoline jumps to match initialization at $0EBE.
Banks in KERNAL and copies the zero-page and work-area images from $0B00-$0DFF back into $0000 and $0200-$03FF. Copies the reload stub from $0E76 to $0334 and executes it there.
Source of the stub installed in low RAM by $0E06 when returning to selection. It blanks the display, sets up the KERNAL file call and transfers control again after the reload.
Masks CPU interrupts, banks out the KERNAL, blanks the screen, disables CIA1 timer interrupts and selects the VIC's $C000 bank before setting up the match vectors.
Points the hardware IRQ at $575B and NMI at $0E85, then clears match flags, stages glyphs from character ROM and prepares the bottom line of text.
Copies the three palette bytes at $EFFD-$EFFF into the VIC registers $D021-$D023.

Iterates the ball and active players, copying each actor's position, rates and flags into zero-page workspace. Players run their control and action handlers and the ball uses its own routine. Dirty fields are copied back as the loop moves to the next actor.
Prints green and blue totals using the scores in $37-$3A and column positions at $3B-$3C.
Takes the low two BCD digits in A and the hundreds digit in X. Suppresses leading zeroes and writes the digits and their colour starting at column Y.
Draws both scores with the alternate decimal printer, whose temporary digit and colour fields live at $15C8-$15CA.
Draws the target prompt and current BCD value. Polls the applicable controller and debounces the choice using the raster countdown at $07AB.
Uses decimal mode to subtract two from the two-byte value at $EA-$EB, then redraws the target. The preceding guard keeps the 2-point minimum.
Uses decimal mode to add two to $EA-$EB. The caller only reaches this branch while the hundreds byte is zero.
Clears the setup prompt, displays the selected target, waits for the countdown and then enters the match loop. Compares both scores against $EA-$EB after each update.
Reads either both joystick ports together or the selected human port, using the match options held at $FF23 and $FF1C.
Stores A in $07AB and waits for it to become negative. The raster handler decrements it.

Prints a zero-terminated string from X:Y at column A in $CFC0 and assigns each cell the colour in $E7. Maps digits to $00-$09, the space to $0A, letters to the match font and punctuation to dedicated indices.
Writes the match font's blank ($0A) across the 40-cell bottom row at $CFC0.
Zero-terminated caption printed while the target score is selected.
Zero-terminated prefix for the target-score announcement after confirmation.
Zero-terminated phrase appended to the winning team's name.
Zero-terminated question asking whether to play again with the same teams.
Clears the action flags at $41-$42 and dispatches from the ball phase at $20. A zero phase returns immediately.
The phase $50 path performs the made-basket setup, calls the scoring routine at $558F and starts a ten-tick follow-up timer.
Chooses a CIA port from the side assignment at $FF1C. Uses the CPU controller when the side flag at $3D is set, otherwise passes the direction bits to the movement decoder.
Uses the opposite port mapping from green and checks $3E before choosing human movement or the CPU controller.
Masks off the fire bit and maps the four direction bits through $2106. Invalid entries take the stationary path.
Dispatches through a jump table selected by $6C. The handler updates SID voice 1 for a sound effect.
Eleven pointers to SID voice 1 effect steps, including the idle RTS.
Clears the gate, sets envelope and starting frequency, then sets gate and noise together and initializes the first sweep countdown.
Adds the signed step $FF88 to the voice 1 frequency, decrements the countdown at $76 and advances the effect after it expires.
Sets up SID voice 2 with noise, envelope and sweep state and advances $6D.

Uses the active slot in X to find a character-specific pointer table at $7002. Selects an overlay record by $031B,X and an underlying pose record by $0322,X, then reads their two-byte placement headers.
Uses the slot and buffer selector at $0771 to patch the copy destinations from $3159, then copies the base-pose bytes in two spans separated by the VIC sprite padding byte.
Picks one of the six sprite templates in file K from the pointer table at $3355 and patches the three indexed loads used for its three byte columns.
Copies 21 rows of the selected template into $F440, mapping each source byte through the lookup table at $0568.
Six 64-byte-aligned source addresses from $FD80 to $FEC0. The caller selects one and patches the three source operands in the recolour loop.

Patches the source of the edge-column copy according to the scroll direction and column. Moves the existing visible cells between the $CC00 and $F000 matrices and fetches the newly exposed column from the two halves at $E000 and $E400.

Copies an edge column using the row-offset table at $362E and the prepatched source and destination in the two indexed instructions. A row flag tells the loop when to increment the high operand bytes.
Waits for a safe raster region, clears two fine-scroll state bytes and marks a matrix change. Copies the selected 40-column colour window one row at a time from the 80-column source at $E800.
Selects a 17-cell column using the pointer table at $468E. Converts the vertical coordinate at $0550 to a row index, reads that map byte and dispatches through the table at $3C91.
Seventy-one little-endian contact handlers. The cell index from the column map at $3C7E selects a destination by patching $3C8E.
Returns carry clear immediately for cell codes such as $00 and $41.
Checks the shared contact guard, then uses $67 to select and order the coordinate corrections around $433B before updating contact and sound.
Partner to the $20-family response. Its correction at $42ED is applied on the opposite side of the coordinate adjustment sequence.
Applies the shared guard and the fixed sequence $4BA9, $433B, $4BD3, then updates contact.
Jumps into the type-$03 response after its first sub-cell test.
Requires $67 below 4 and the shared guard before applying correction $437C and updating contact.
Uses the same four-unit sub-cell guard with the correction at $43D0.
Performs the $42ED correction between the two coordinate adjustments and then updates contact.
Calls the $42ED correction directly once the contact guard succeeds.
Tests which side of a sloped boundary the in-cell coordinates in $66 and $67 fall on. Selects a correction path according to ball height.
Tests the complementary in-cell slope, using ball height to distinguish its lower and upper responses.
Records contact, selects effect 1 and adds one to the ball's integer Y coordinate.
Compares ball height with $38 before allowing the positive X correction. Below that height it selects the carry-set result at $40FE.
Records the hit, starts effect 1 and increments the ball's horizontal coordinate, propagating carry to its high byte.
Selects among six 16-byte response shapes. Each small entry chooses its shape and passes the result to the common routine at $3F6F.
Six 16-byte lookup sequences selected by the shape-specific cell handlers at $3ED4-$3F3F.
Checks the same ball-height boundary as cell $45 before allowing the negative X correction.
Records the hit and subtracts one from the two-byte ball X coordinate while CPU interrupts are masked.
Returns carry clear when the high vertical delta is negative. Otherwise assigns result 1 at $21 and returns carry set.
Tests the high and low vertical delta, assigns result 2 and returns carry set when the paired condition is met.
Stores result 0 at $21 and returns carry set.
When both ball height and a vertical rate field are negative, samples the SID oscillator and calls the effect twice on one in four low-bit results.
Eighty little-endian column pointers at 17-byte intervals into $C000-$C54F. The contact lookup selects the column from the horizontal coordinate.

Iterates the six players and ball, applying accumulated coordinate deltas. Patches the immediate sign byte at $4767 before adding the fractional and integer X steps to the actor position. Clamps the resulting court coordinates.
Uses ball state, slot state and the SID oscillator readout to choose a timer or movement for a computer-controlled actor. Active timers can return before the remaining steering calculations.
Adds two in decimal mode to the appropriate two-byte score at $37-$38 or $39-$3A. The XOR of $21 and $1F selects the team. Refreshes scores and advances the ball phase.

Reads a scheduled line from $03C3 and an operation from $03DB. Flagged operations set a sprite's Y coordinate and the others update its pointers in both screen matrices. On exhaustion it restores $575B and sets the next IRQ to raster $F0.
Restores the main raster vector at $FFFE-$FFFF and sets $D012 to $F0 before acknowledging the IRQ and returning.

Dispatches on the raster line. During the split near $F1 it selects the score font at $D000 and blanks the background, then schedules line $FB. At the later interrupt it restores the court view and updates sprites and match work.
Restores the court background from $EFFD, installs fine X scroll and multicolour mode, selects the active screen matrix and updates the raster tick at $E1.
For a positive queue index in $E0, installs IRQ $56F8 and schedules the first entry one raster line before its target.
Uses the active actor index at $D7 to read its state from $0200 and patch the destination of the jump at $5BA7. The selected handler updates the slot for the sprite compositor.
A 24-entry little-endian jump table indexed by the actor state in the pose update at $5B94.
Clears the first $2F VIC registers, sets $D011 and $D018 for a blank display and assigns background colour 1.

Uses the team index and difficulty-dependent thresholds at $69DA and $69E3 to compare a cached SID oscillator sample. Can discard the immediate return address to bypass the remainder of the steering routine or choose a random movement path.
Six little-endian pointers selected by the drafted players. The compositor at $2CF0 uses the slot to choose a pointer, then uses the overlay index at $031B,X to find a record in that catalogue.
Little-endian base-pose addresses indexed through the slot's pose selector at $0322. The compositor reads a placement header from the chosen record and copies its body, skipping sprite padding.

80 consecutive columns of 17 cell codes for the school court. The column pointers start at $468E; the contact lookup at $3C7E uses the code to dispatch to tile-specific logic.
The final 20 columns in the 80-by-17 contact map. Values are dispatched through $3C91 by the court contact lookup.
Court character patterns for codes $00-$7F. The VIC fetches eight bytes per character from this bank during the display phase with memory pointer $36.
Second half of the same court character bank. The VIC sees these bytes in RAM under the CIA addresses while CPU accesses there reach the chips with I/O visible.
